full_judgment:
Sikder Maqbul Huq, J: This rule was issued calling upon the pre-emptor Opposite Party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 15.9.1993 allowing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1987 by the learned Additional District Judge, Gazipur, reversing the judgment and order dated 13.5.1987 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Kaliakoir, Gazipur, in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1986 should not be set aside. 

 2. Pre-emptor Opposite Party No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1986 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kaliakoir, Gazipur for pre-emption of the case land contending inter-alia that she is a co-sharer in the disputed holding and pre emptee Opposite Party No. 1 is a stranger thereto and that she is legally entitled to pre-empt the case land. 

 3. Present petitioners, being Opposite Party Nos. 1 and 2 in the Miscellaneous Case, filed a joint written objection denying the material allegations of the petitioner and contending inter-alia that Opposite Party No. 2 executed a sale deed on 28.10.1995 in respect of the case land and other land in favour of petitioner No. 1 who simultaneously executed a deed of agreement to reconvey the land in favour of the vendor Opposite Party No. 2 on repayment of the consideration money within 5 years and the disputed transfer is not a sale out and out but a mortgage with a conditional sale. 

 4. The learned trial court disallowed the Miscellaneous case on finding that the vendor Opposite Party No. 2 has transferred the case land to the pre-emptee opposite Party No. 1 who has purchased the same with an agreement to reconvey on repayment of the consideration money within 5 years. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the trial court, the pre-emptor preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1987 before the learned District Judge, Gazipur and the appeal was transferred for disposal to the learned Additional District Judge, Gazipur and he, after hearing both the sides, allowed the same. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the learned court of appeal below, Opposite Party Nos. 1 and 2 of the Miscellaneous case have preferred the instant revisional application. 

 8. Mr. Ahmed Ali Mondal, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that the disputed transfer is a mortgage in view of the circumstantial evidence particularly when P.W.2 stated in his cross-examination that price of one decimal of land may be Taka 15/16 thousand whereas the consideration of the case land measuring 33 decimals has been shown as Tk. 4,000/- in the disputed deed and that the learned court of appeal below was not legally justified in holding that the transaction is a sale out and out and as such committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order allowing the appeal and the Miscellaneous Case as well. 

 9. Mr. A.B.M. Abbas Uddin, the learned advocate appearing for the pre-emptee opposite party, on the other hand, submits that the learned court of appeal below, after considering the facts and circumstances of the case, came to a finding that subsequent transaction in favour of vendor Opposite Party No. 2 in the name of reconveyance is a mere paper transaction and committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.The learned advocate further submits that the learned court of appeal below reversed the findings of the trial court with reference to material evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case and as such committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned advocate further submits that the alleged deed of agreement has been subsequently fabricated on previously purchased stamp papers with a view to defeat the right of pre-emption. 

 11. There is no dispute about the fact that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the disputed holding and the pre-emptee Opposite Party no. 1 is a stranger thereto. There is also no dispute about the fact that the application for pre-emption was filed well within time and the pre-emptor is otherwise entitled to pre-empt the case land. The learned advocate appearing for the petitioner referring to the decision in the case of Abbas Ali Vs. Osman Ali reported in 37 DLR page 324 submits that in the vent of revonveyance of the land under pre-emption to the vendor there remains no sale and as such no cause for pre-emption would arise. In the said reported case the case land in pursuance of an agreement of rconveyance was recoveyed to the vendor before filing of the pre-emption case but the case before me is otherwise and thus the aforesaid case is quite distinguishable and this has been also considered by the learned Additional District Judge in his impugned judgment and order. 

 12. It appears from the record that the learned court of appeal below did not give any finding regarding the alleged deed of record arrived at a finding to the effect that pre-emptee opposite party purchased the case land with an agreement for reconveyance as alleged. The court of appeal below simply fond in his judgment that the transaction of reconveyance immediately after judgment and order of the trial court is colourable one only because it has been made after disposal of the Miscellaneous Case by the learned trial court. A transaction does not become colourable only because it has been made after the disposal of an application for pre-emption by the trial court or even by any other superior court. It further appears from the record that neither of the P.W.s denied the alleged agreement for reconveyance in his deposition and the learned Additional District Judge failed to consider this aspect of the case. It may, in this connection, further be mentioned that the learned Additional District Judge did not at all advert to the evidence of the witnesses regarding the agreement for reconveyance and he also did not reverse the findings of the trial court in this regard. Evidence on record supports the findings of the learned trial court. Thus it is found that the learned Additional District Judge was not legally justified in passing the impugned order and he committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
